In 1980 John Grant wrote to the Minister for Sport advocating for a national policy on sport for people with disabilities [d37675808s4p0].
The Australian Government subsequently established a national advisory committee on sports for disabled persons and John Grant was a member of that committee [d37675808s4p0].

sub_answers.text: In 1980 John Grant wrote to the Minister for Sport, Bob Ellicott, stating the case for a national policy on sport for people with disabilities [d37675808s4p0]. The Australian Government subsequently established a national advisory committee on sports for disabled persons and John Grant was a member of that committee [d37675808s4p0].

sub_answers.text: John Grant was instrumental in establishing the Junior National Wheelchair Games while he was president of the Paraplegic and Quadriplegic Association of New South Wales [d37675808s4p0]. Grant played a major role in organising the First Royal North Shore Hospital Games for spinal injury patients in 1958 and included sports in rehabilitation programs at Mount Wilga House, which held annual Sports Days [d37675808s4p0].

sub_answers.text: The Paralympics grouped athlete disabilities into five broad categories: amputation, cerebral palsy, wheelchair users, visual impairment and Les autres (other physical disabilities). [d25711178s1p0]  Each Paralympic sport used its own sport-specific classification system with event codes describing the event type and athlete classification, including standing classes LW1–LW9 and sitting classes LW10–LW12 in winter sports. [d25711178s1p0]  The International Paralympic Committee oversaw classification and classification was based on functional disability criteria. [d33211794s1p0][d36583541s5p0]  In para-swimming functional criteria were assessed to assign athletes to classes S1–S10 and additional classes existed for visual impairment (S11–S13) and intellectual disability (S14), with stroke-specific and functional considerations used in assigning classes. [d36583541s1p0]
